claims: The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission is scheduled to splash down at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
The Orion capsule will enter the atmosphere at 4:53 p.m. PDT.
Recovery teams are positioned to retrieve the four astronauts shortly after.
The splashdown location is the Pacific Ocean 45-80 miles off the San Diego coast.
Live coverage is available on NASA YouTube, NASA+, and the NASA App.
The Orion capsule will undergo a "fireball" reentry through the atmosphere.
Parachute deployment will occur shortly before impact.
The crew will be recovered by the USS John P. Murtha.
